one_line: AI-assisted refund exception investigation with human-approved recovery.
what_it_does: Investigates orders, returns, and refund status, prepares escalation/recovery, and requires explicit human approval before consequential submission.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools make multi-system refund investigation and shared human approval more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description name tools for finding orders, inspecting returns/refunds, preparing escalation, and verifying the case.
Contact sheet visibly includes refund-focused product surfaces and an AI workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent refund workflow and visible product surfaces, but the contact sheet does not clearly show the complete end-to-end approval and recovery result.
execution_evidence: Product-motion contact sheet shows an AI/content surface and a refund-themed web product.
Description specifies investigation, preparation, approval, and verification stages.
impact_rationale: Refund exceptions are a concrete operational problem for merchants and customers, and the proposed human gate addresses risk while reducing tedious investigation.
impact_evidence: Description identifies verified returns with missing refunds as the target problem.
Workflow is aimed at safe recovery rather than unsupervised financial action.
creativity_rationale: The human-controlled refund-recovery collaboration is a strong, practical WebMCP application with a meaningful trust boundary.
creativity_evidence: Combines agent investigation with explicit approval and post-action verification.
Frames connect refund operations to structured browser tools.
usability_note: Clear operational flow and approval boundary; end-to-end usability is not fully visible.
red_flags: No transcript and small contact-sheet text limit verification of exact tool calls.
standouts: Consequential-action approval is central rather than cosmetic.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and credible operational value, with a coherent product concept despite partial visual proof.

one_line: Browser-native command center that plans, recovers, and documents an event launch.

leverage_rationale: The shared tool registry, live state, recovery path, approvals, and connected exports make WebMCP central to the demonstrated collaboration.
leverage_evidence: Contact sheet visibly shows Tool Registry connected to venue, Slack, menu, handoff, invites, and budget nodes.
Frames show Ready state, operational changes, human approval, and WebMCP-as-unlock messaging.
Description specifies injected constraint change and recovery without increasing budget.
execution_rationale: The central workflow is unusually well specified and visually evidenced from planning through recovery, approval, and handoff outputs.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows event dashboard with Atlas Beta Launch Night, 40 attendees, $2,500 budget, tool graph, and approval state.
Description names runbook, Calendar/ICS, email, Slack Block Kit, and automation JSON outputs.
impact_rationale: Event planners and operations teams can obtain credible value from constraint-aware planning and reusable handoffs.
impact_evidence: Concrete launch-night planning scenario with fixed budget and menu constraints.
Connected outputs target real team coordination systems.
creativity_rationale: The surprise-surge recovery scenario and connected handoff make a memorable, ambitious agent interaction rather than a chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Agent must recover from a new VIP surge while preserving budget and menu direction.
Tool graph and multi-format handoff pursue the concept deeply.
usability_note: The dashboard communicates state and approval clearly, though small frame text limits detailed inspection.
standouts: Visible tool registry and recovery narrative.
Approval plus exportable handoff gives the run a durable result.
advance_reason: Top-tier evidence-backed WebMCP leverage, execution, and ambition.

one_line: Supervised WebMCP agent command center with policy-based risk gates.
what_it_does: Runs low-risk web actions automatically, pauses consequential actions for approval, and blocks credentials, password changes, and transfers.
leverage_rationale: A structured policy layer can classify and gate tool calls before execution, a materially stronger boundary than pixel automation.
leverage_evidence: Contact sheet shows command center, task policy, audit log, mission cards, and approval-oriented controls.
Description distinguishes low-risk automatic actions from approval and never-auto-approved categories.
execution_rationale: The concept and command-center surface are coherent, but visible frames show mostly plans/pending tasks rather than a fully completed mission.
execution_evidence: Frames show Give AI the web/Keep yourself in control dashboard with task cards and policy/audit navigation.
Description defines risk score, approval, and audit behavior.
impact_rationale: Safe delegation of browsing, booking, purchases, and messaging is a real need for users concerned about agent overreach.
impact_evidence: Concrete examples include flights, pizza orders, bookings, purchases, and messages.
Hard blocks target high-consequence actions.
creativity_rationale: The explicit middle ground between full autonomy and approval of every click is a strong interaction and trust model.
creativity_evidence: Sentinel trust/policy layer is structural and risk-aware.
Command center combines mission planning with human control.
usability_note: Mission and policy concepts are legible, but completed task feedback is only partly visible.
red_flags: Contact sheet does not clearly prove a completed external action.
standouts: Risk-tiered approval model is clear and relevant.
advance_reason: High-value agent safety concept with visible command-center evidence.

one_line: Accessible football scores and fixtures through direct agent requests.
what_it_does: Lets fans browse, filter, follow, and ask an agent for fixtures and scores without navigating dense sports pages.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a direct structured route through dense sports information, especially useful for screen-reader and voice users, though the same data can be queried by other means.
leverage_evidence: Description gives concrete requests for Liverpool, AFC Telford, Scottish competitions, and followed teams.
Contact sheet visibly shows the Matchday landing surface but not tool invocation.
execution_rationale: The product identity and accessibility goal are clear, but the viewed frames remain largely on an idle landing state and do not demonstrate the query workflow end to end.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows repeated Matchday/WebMCP Challenge landing screens.
Description specifies browse, search, filters, favourites, and agent requests.
impact_rationale: The targeted accessibility problem is concrete and personal, and reducing navigation burden can materially improve access to a beloved hobby.
impact_evidence: Description explains dense sports pages and long screen-reader navigation for blind fans.
Specific intended user example is an 80-year-old blind football supporter.
creativity_rationale: The combination of a conventional sports site with a direct agent route for smaller clubs is a thoughtful accessibility-focused angle.
creativity_evidence: Complements rather than replaces the accessible interface.
Supports flexible club, competition, date-range, and followed-team requests.
usability_note: Familiar sports layout plus direct queries should be approachable; the contact sheet does not show results.
red_flags: Frames show an idle landing state, not the stated agent interaction.
advance_reason: Strong impact and clear purpose, with execution evidence limited to the landing state.

one_line: Browser execution firewall with deterministic risk and cryptographic audit controls.
what_it_does: Freezes risky WebMCP calls pending human authorization, applies policies, and records SHA-256-linked audit evidence.
leverage_rationale: A browser-bound execution firewall and tamper-evident ledger change what agent tool execution can safely guarantee beyond ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies deterministic risk engine, human-in-the-loop authorization, and SHA-256 audit chain.
Contact sheet visibly shows Uranus dashboard, dynamic policy, and cryptographic audit-chain surfaces.
execution_rationale: The security workflow is coherent and the dashboard surfaces are visible, but the frames do not fully prove a blocked call, approval, and ledger verification sequence.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows repeated dashboard, dynamic policy, and cryptographic audit-chain views.
Description identifies indirect prompt injection, runaway loops, and absence-of-proof threats.
impact_rationale: Preventing unauthorized financial or state-changing agent actions is a credible need for organizations deploying browser agents.
impact_evidence: Targeted risks include payouts, balances, transfers, and persistent mutations.
Human approval and cryptographic proof address consequential operations.
creativity_rationale: The perpendicular execution-freeze framing and cryptographic non-repudiation are ambitious additions to WebMCP safety UX.
creativity_evidence: Combines policy enforcement with an audit chain rather than relying on prompts.
Dashboard exposes policy and ledger as product features.
usability_note: Security surfaces are visible, but the operational path is dense and only partially demonstrated.
red_flags: Cryptographic claims are described but not independently verifiable from contact sheets.
standouts: Execution firewall plus tamper-evident audit trail.
advance_reason: Meaningful agent-infrastructure contribution with strong safety rationale.

one_line: An agent points to the next UI control so users can learn rather than hand over access.
what_it_does: Uses a site's interface map to highlight where the user should click for a requested setting or task, without taking over the account.
leverage_rationale: Structured interface maps let the agent provide precise, on-screen guidance without unreliable visual clicking or credential handoff.
leverage_evidence: Description contrasts pointing at the user's screen with an agent executing settings changes.
Contact sheet shows ShowMe documentation/demo alongside a financial dashboard and developer console.
execution_rationale: The instructional concept and supporting documentation are visible, but the contact sheet does not clearly show an actual highlighted target or completed guided task.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly include ShowMe instructional pages, code/configuration snippets, and a dashboard context.
Description specifies the ask, interface map, pointer, and user click loop.
impact_rationale: Many users struggle to locate settings in complex apps; teaching them while preserving account control has credible value.
impact_evidence: Description cites Auth0, Jira, and Datadog navigation problems.
User remains the actor, reducing trust and security concerns.
creativity_rationale: The learn-by-pointing interaction is a fresh alternative to both help articles and autonomous agents.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly aims to reduce future dependence by teaching the location.
Uses agent capability for guidance rather than takeover.
usability_note: The intended interaction is simple and user-controlled; proof of the pointer state is incomplete.
red_flags: Contact sheet emphasizes documentation and mixed development views over the core pointer result.
standouts: Preserves user agency while solving interface discoverability.
advance_reason: Original, user-respecting guidance model with moderate visual proof.

one_line: A shared four-bar beat canvas for human and agent composition.
what_it_does: Lets people and agents read musical state, set tempo/key, write instrument patterns, humanize, audition, and save reusable beats.
leverage_rationale: Structured musical state and layer-level writing let an agent collaborate inside the timeline with precision that UI clicking would make cumbersome.
leverage_evidence: Description enumerates tools for state reading, tempo/key, drums, melodies, chords, humanization, playback, and patterns.

Sequential auditioning makes agent contributions visible and audible in the intended experience.

Visible frames do not clearly show completed beat playback.

one_line: Private in-browser video editor that an agent can optimize through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Inspects timeline and transcript, removes dead air, places relevant footage, trims and zooms clips, and optimizes duration without uploading files.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to timeline, transcript, constraints, and edit operations enables precise multi-step editing while preserving local media and shared manual/agent history.
leverage_evidence: Description lists inspect, detect dead air, transcript search, placement, trimming, zoom, and duration optimization tools.
Description reports one optimize_duration call reducing a 108.7-second edit to 60 seconds.
Contact sheet visibly shows an editor/workflow with prompt, inspector, timeline/status area, and menu state.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and unusually concrete, with a target runtime, transcript alignment, activity feed, and shared history; frames show editor states but not a fully legible final export.
execution_evidence: Description gives specific activity entries including removed dead air, dropped narration, transcript match, and placed terminal recording.
Contact sheet shows multi-panel editor, inspector, timeline, and configured states.
impact_rationale: Creators regularly face tedious transcript-aligned trimming, and local processing addresses privacy concerns for unreleased footage.
impact_evidence: Description identifies repetitive dead-air removal and footage alignment as the target pain.
Nothing uploads, which matters for private product recordings.
creativity_rationale: Combining local-first editing, transcript-aware placement, duration optimization, and unified manual/agent history is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits inside the browser tab rather than a server-side black box.
Manual and agent actions share one plain-English activity feed.
usability_note: Target and activity feedback are clear; final export proof is not fully visible.
red_flags: Contact-sheet text is small, so exact final edit state is not independently legible.
standouts: Concrete measurable duration optimization and local privacy story.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with credible creator impact and strong execution evidence.

one_line: Constraint-aware carbon scheduling where humans and agents agree on tradeoffs.
what_it_does: Plans workloads against carbon and cost forecasts, explains infeasibility, proposes single-constraint trades, and produces an execution contract.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a shared stateful negotiation surface where agents can plan, explain conflicts, and obtain explicit acceptance without silently changing locked constraints.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes live state changes, locks, recomputation, and accept/reject tradeoffs.
Contact sheet shows a dashboard/editor progression from prompt to configuration to scored recommendation and charts.
execution_rationale: The constraint-solver story is coherent and the contact sheet visibly reaches a recommendation dashboard with metrics and chart output, though exact agent calls are small.
execution_evidence: Frames show empty prompt, requirements/configuration form, then recommendation with metrics and trend chart.
Description specifies 24-hour bundled forecasts and named infeasibility explanations.
impact_rationale: Operators have a real need to reduce carbon while preserving region, cost, and deadlines; explicit tradeoffs improve trust in scheduling.
impact_evidence: Concrete example trades 45 minutes for 38% reduction while preserving region and cost.
Output is a carbon execution contract recording preserved and relaxed constraints.
creativity_rationale: Turning infeasibility into explainable, smallest-trade negotiation is an original and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Solver tracks which constraint killed each window.
Locked constraints and one-constraint trades are central product mechanics.
usability_note: Recommendation, metrics, and chart make tradeoffs legible; small text limits exact inspection.
red_flags: Exact WebMCP invocation is not legible in the contact sheet.
standouts: Explainable infeasibility and explicit human-negotiated tradeoffs.
advance_reason: Strong real-world value and unusually thoughtful constraint negotiation.

impact_evidence: Description identifies product engineers and client/agency dashboard workflows.
